intermediate is stored **uncompressed** (570.4 MB per tile, 4.97 TB per dense cell), which is what
sets the duration; compressing it is the only change that would move assembly wall-clock
materially.

**The trailing-assembly thread is not the critical path at the planned fleet width** — 11 minutes
of tail on an ~8-day campaign — but the margin is 21% and it is an **actor ceiling of ~275 per
cluster**, not a property of assembly. Inference per tile falls as actors rise while assembly does
not, so they cross. The consequence is a coupling nobody chose: **the 85%-provisioning policy is
the only thing holding the campaign under that ceiling**, so fleet width and assembly capacity
cannot be decided independently.

### Instrumentation that was reporting nothing useful

A dense zone-year's assembly ran for over three hours emitting `0/16 band writes done` and nothing
else. Three separate causes: the coordinator reports *completions* of round-robin partitions that
all finish within six minutes of each other; the worker body logged nothing at all; and a
**spawned worker inherits no logging configuration**, so worker lines would have been silently
discarded even once written. The coordinator's line also never reached the Prefect UI, because
`shard_writer` was left on its module logger while `assembly` threads the flow's run logger down.
All fixed, with the two-level routing invariant stated where it can be read.

### Published data now records what it lost

Skipped tiles — every pixel failed the validity filter — were written as **fill** and the year
marked complete. Fill is also what ocean reads as, so a consumer could not distinguish "no valid
optical data" from "not land": roughly 7,100 km² in one cell and 39,000 km² in another. Comparing
two independent fills showed the skipped sets are **byte-identical and spatially contiguous**, so
these are real coverage gaps rather than flaky workers.

`optical_skips` now records the count, the labels and the live total per year, following the
argument that already justifies `radar_coverage`: coverage is a property of what was acquired, not
of the terrain. It is built from the **staging prefix**, not the finishing leg — skip markers
persist across resumes, so a leg that staged nothing for tiles an earlier leg skipped would report
them as successes and record zero skips while publishing fill over them.

### Recovery, drilled rather than argued

A hard kill of the flow body — every `finally` and context manager skipped — recovered a five-instance
Ray fleet in **about three seconds** via the crash hook. This **refutes** the claim that Prefect
runs terminal hooks in the flow's own process: they run in the surviving one. The consequence is
that the orphan-fleet sweep's lack of any EC2 path, while real, is **not on the recovery path**,
so extending it is not justified on current evidence.

A commit slot held by a killed process returns unaided after **302 s** by lease expiry, so there is
no manual release procedure to write.

### One uncertainty deliberately carried

The 35–50° latitude band is **interpolated, not measured**, and measuring it is decided against as
too expensive for what it buys. It remains the widest single driver of the cost interval: if the
true depth there sits at the top of the measured 66–152 spread the line is understated across
19.2% of campaign land. Recorded as a decision so it is not revived as an open question.


---

## Added since — 2026-08-10

### A deterministic catalogue refusal, diagnosed rather than waited out

One zone-year's optical search returned HTTP 502 every time, defeating nine HTTP attempts across
364 s of backoff and recurring identically hours apart. It had already stopped two pieces of work,
and everything pointed at the archive.

**It was a page-size sensitivity, and the fix was ours.** Holding the bounding box, client,
credentials and retry ladder fixed, the query refuses at **250 items per page** and answers in under
two seconds at **100**, while the adjacent year answers at 250 without trouble. Earth Search's page
size is now 100, set **per provider** rather than on the shared default — raising it for CMR-STAC
made that catalogue's 500s worse, so this is a property of one service, not a rule about page sizes.

Two supporting changes came out of the same investigation:

- **`catalogue_refusal.py` names the failing request** and separates a refusal that retrying can
  clear from one it cannot, so a deterministic refusal stops paying for the ladder.
- **The retry budget is now bounded in wall clock (36 h), because only attempt *counts* ever were.**
  A single page fetch is already 9 HTTP attempts over 364 s that every outer layer counts as one
  try, and those budgets multiply — up to 12 leg dispatches. The bound is checked when an attempt
  *starts*, so it never interrupts work in flight.

### The two failures no operator can produce by hand

Two Phase 5 drills could not reach the failures they name. The mid-commit death occupies a gap
bounded by two commits of one function — **37 s at the end of a ~196-minute assembly** on a dense
cell, milliseconds on a small one — so no external kill lands there reliably. The starvation
tripwire needs a fleet alive and holding nothing, which every healthy mechanism removes as soon as
it appears. A drill that misses its own failure reports a **false pass**, which is worse than
leaving the question open, so both are now injected from inside the run under an explicit request.

One of the two sits on the commit path of the store that is the campaign's only output, so
"cannot fire unasked" is **structural rather than careful**:

| guard | what it stops |
|---|---|
| a flow parameter defaulting to nothing, and **never an environment variable** | a value left in a task definition or an image being inherited by an ordinary run |
| an injection site accepts only an `ArmedFault`, and the arming call is its sole constructor (pinned by a syntax-tree test) | any path to a firing site that skipped the checks |
| arming refuses every deployment outside an **allowlist** naming `global-tessera-dev` | production, `yield`, and a run whose deployment identity does not resolve — which is what a mis-registered production run looks like |
| each flow declares which fault it hosts; the other is refused | an armed drill quietly injecting nothing and being written up as a pass |
| the death must name its cell; the hold must state a length, bounded at 45 min | a multi-cell run losing a cell the drill was not aimed at, and an unbounded hold on a fleet nothing reclaims |

Identity is **read**, never asked for — off the Ray control-plane prefix a registration injects — so
a flow cannot claim an account of its own choosing. An armed run announces itself at error level
under a fixed prefix, twice, so a drill's artifacts are never read as an incident.

**One defect the tests caught before any fleet did.** The withholding fault first inspected its work
source's result. A hand-over *removes* the zone from the feeder's queue, so that version **deleted**
prepared work instead of delaying it — a runner test failed with one cell filled out of two. It now
takes the source as a callable and simply does not call it while holding, which makes
non-consumption a property of the shape rather than a rule someone must remember.


## Added since — 2026-08-12

### A landed cell is handed to a validator, and nothing waits for it

Both fill flows take a `validation_deployment` and create one run of it per cell the moment that
cell's zone-year tag exists (`flows/_cell_validation.py`). On the chained path the dispatch rides the
**trailing assembly thread**, so cell N is validated while cell N+1 is still inferring — the same
pipelining assembly already has — and `timeout=0` means the campaign never waits on the result.

The validator itself is a consumer's flow; this library names none, so the default is `None` and,
unlike every other child ref here, it is **not derived from `branch`**. A consumer names it at
registration, where a wrong or absent value is visible before a campaign runs rather than a thousand
cells later.

Three decisions worth stating, each closing a way this goes wrong:

- **A cell that fails validation is already tagged**, deliberately. Withholding the tag until a
  separate run agrees would make campaign progress depend on a run it does not wait for, and a
  validation that never ran would then look exactly like a cell that never landed. So the tag says
  the cell **LANDED** and the verdict says it is **SOUND** — different questions, different records.
- **Every dispatch failure is swallowed.** A landed, tagged cell must not be undone by an unreachable
  API. What keeps that honest is not the log line but the verdict: a dispatch that never happened
  leaves none, and the consumer's monitoring reads published cells against the verdicts on file.
- **An unset validator is omitted from the dispatch, not forwarded as `None`.** Every other setting
  the campaign hands a fill is forwarded unconditionally, which is right when the campaign is the
  authority; here it is not. Forwarding `None` would override a correctly-registered ref with nothing
  and run a whole campaign unvalidated while every deployment still looked configured.

An empty cell is declined — nothing was embedded, so every pixel check has no subject — which matches
the closing sweep's own exclusion. The two passes have to agree about what the validated set *is*, or
monitoring reads one pass's deliberate exclusion as the other's missing verdict.

**Why the fill dispatches this itself rather than an automation firing on completion:** Prefect's
event broker is in-memory and drops events under load, and we have measured it declaring healthy runs
dead. An event-driven trigger would therefore skip cells silently and at random — precisely the cells
filled while the server was busiest.

Verified end to end on `global-tessera-dev` against a real cell: 12 seconds, figures and verdict
published, 13 checks passing.

### Two campaign design records updated

**`campaign-plan.md` §3b** now describes what shipped rather than what was planned, including why the
tag is no longer withheld and that nothing retries or reopens a failed cell automatically. Its watch
list gains the missing-verdict row: a published cell with no verdict means nothing checked it.

**`campaign-monitoring-plan.md`** is new. It starts from the constraint rather than from a dashboard —
the campaign cannot be stopped cheaply and has almost no surgical fix — so monitoring exists to
produce one of three decisions: **stop everything** (only affordable in the first hours), **shelve the
zone for a second wave** (the common case, whose whole product is a list of named zones), or
**ignore**. A signals-to-decision table built from the checks that exist, a 5-minute cron round with a
two-tier cadence that keeps the measured monitoring cost at ~$5/day rather than $16, and a first-day
protocol whose most valuable reading is the **T+1 h validation verdict** — the first time anything
says whether the pixels are right, for three minutes and three cents, and the only stop-everything
signal available before real money is spent. Nothing in it is built yet.

items.title: Remote tmux (`-CC` over SSH) mirroring (beta)
items.body: > [!NOTE] > **Dependency resolved** — manaflow-ai/bonsplit#143 (the `didReorderTabsInPane` > delegate this PR's tab/window reorder sync relies on) is merged, and > `vendor/bonsplit` is pinned to the merged upstream `main` SHA (`5728c21`). > This branch builds standalone. **What this adds** An opt-in beta that drives a remote `tmux` session from cmux over SSH using tmux control mode (`tmux -CC`). Instead of a plain SSH terminal, the remote session is reprojected into cmux's native UI — workspaces, tabs, splits, scrollback, copy — and cmux drives the real tmux server behind it. Off by default (Settings → Beta Features → Remote tmux), so local terminals are unchanged. ## Demo https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7fddf6d9-cb53-49c6-b545-13c3672926c6 **The model mapping (the core of it)** cmux and tmux nest layouts in opposite directions: in cmux a **pane** holds a row of **tabs** (each tab = one terminal); in tmux a **window** holds a split of **panes**. This bridges them: | tmux | cmux | |---|---| | session | a workspace in the sidebar | | window | a tab in that workspace | | pane | a pane in a native split **inside that tab** | The new capability is **panes inside a tab**: a cmux tab previously held a single terminal, but a multi-pane tmux window is now rendered as a real cmux split layout within one tab (each remote pane is a native cmux terminal pane with the usual chrome). The bridge is **two-way** — splitting/closing a pane in that tab runs tmux `split-window`, and drag-reordering the tabs reorders the tmux windows with `swap-window`. *`tmux ls` on the left, the cmux sidebar on the right — each session becomes a workspace, each window a tab.* *A tmux window's panes render as a native cmux split inside one tab (left: native tmux; right: cmux).* **Using it** Run **`cmux ssh-tmux `** in a terminal — a `~/.ssh/config` alias or `user@host` (optional `--port`, `--identity`, `--no-focus`). cmux opens a new window mirroring that host's tmux sessions (sessions → workspaces, windows → tabs, multi-pane windows → in-tab splits). Auth is hands-off when it can be: discovery runs over a shared SSH ControlMaster in `BatchMode` (no prompt), so key/agent hosts attach with no interaction. If the host needs interactive auth (password, host-key confirmation, MFA, security-key touch), cmux runs `ssh` **inline in your terminal** so you can authenticate, then mirrors the sessions over the now-open connection. `~/.ssh/config` (IdentityFile/ProxyJump/Port) is honored. For finer control, the `remote.tmux.*` socket commands are available (e.g. `remote.tmux.mirror` mirrors a host's sessions into the current window's sidebar instead of a dedicated window). ```bash cmux ssh-tmux dev@example.com cmux ssh-tmux my-ssh-alias --port 2222 --identity ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 ``` Off by default — turn it on in **Settings → Beta Features → Remote tmux**. **How it works** cmux spawns `ssh … tmux -CC attach` and parses the control-mode stream itself (`RemoteTmuxControlStreamParser`) rather than relying on a built-in tmux viewer, so the protocol and `%begin/%end` command correlation are fully owned by cmux. Each remote pane renders into a ghostty manual-I/O surface fed by `%output`; input (keys + mouse) is forwarded with `send-keys -H`. The remote tmux server owns pane sizing/reflow; cmux stays in lock-step and never reflows locally. **Supported behaviors** - **Sizing** — remote client resized to the rendered grid (`refresh-client -C`), so TUIs aren't stuck at 80×24. - **Splits / reorder** — `split-window` and `swap-window` propagation (above). - **Working directory** — remote `pane_current_path` tracked and shown on the tab. - **Rename** — renaming a tab runs tmux `rename-window`, so the name syncs to the remote (and other clients). - **Paste & drop** — single-line content via tmux `paste-buffer -p`, so images arrive as `[Image #N]` (a real bracketed paste). - **Mouse** — click/scroll/drag reach the remote app; Shift+drag for native cmux copy. - **Unicode-correct output** — multi-byte chars survive being split across `%output` updates. - **Live reconnect** — a transient SSH/network drop keeps the mirror frozen and re-attaches automatically with capped exponential backoff (the remote tmux server outlives the control client). On reconnect each pane re-seeds — re-applies the client grid (`refresh-client -C`), re-captures contents with scrollback, re-subscribes cwd — so the session resumes in place. The mirror ends only on a genuine tmux `%exit`, or when a reconnect reaches the host but the session is gone (detected from ssh/tmux stderr); reconnect is attach-only, so a session killed during the outage is never silently recreated. - **Scrollback on attach** — an attached tab seeds the pane's history (`capture-pane -e -S`), so it's scrollable immediately, not only for output printed after attaching. Alt-screen TUIs correctly have no scrollback. - **Out-of-band reorder** — reordering windows on the remote (a second tmux client, or `move-window` / a mid-list `new-window`) reorders the cmux tabs to match, preserving the current tab's focus/selection. - **Disconnect cleanup** — when a host's session genuinely ends, its dedicated remote window closes — gated so it never discards local workspaces (or another host's mirror) moved into it, never leaves zero windows, and degrades a sole window to a fresh local workspace. **Surface** — Beta Features toggle, the **`cmux ssh-tmux`** CLI command, and `remote.tmux.*` socket commands. Docs page added at `/docs/remote-tmux`. **Tests** — auth (stderr classifier / SSH argv policy / connection-keying), control-stream parser, pane-state seeding, and session/layout parser unit tests (Swift Testing). **Dependency — manaflow-ai/bonsplit#143 (merged).** The window/tab reorder sync relies on the `didReorderTabsInPane` delegate added in that PR. `vendor/bonsplit` is pinned to the merged upstream `main` SHA (`5728c21`), which also includes the divider-thickness work (manaflow-ai/bonsplit#139) already on bonsplit `main`. **Known limitations** - **No "reconnecting" indicator** — a transient drop is handled silently (the mirror freezes, then resumes). There's no visual badge while offline, and actions taken during the outage (rename/close/split a tab, keystrokes) are dropped and need re-doing after reconnect. - **Multi-line paste** isn't delivered as one bracketed paste — only single-line content is; multi-line text is sent as plain keystrokes. - **Live cwd updates** need control-mode subscriptions (tmux 3.2+); older tmux shows the initial folder only. - **Scrollback re-wrap on resize** is conditional: shell panes re-wrap; panes running a TUI keep their old wrap (the app repaints its visible frame itself on resize). - **Out-of-band reorder vs. an in-progress local drag** — a remote reorder landing mid tab-drag is a narrow, self-healing cosmetic glitch (the final order reconciles on drop). ## Related issues - Part of #2673 — delivers remote tmux (`-CC`) mirroring over SSH ControlMaster (the broader remote-workspace routing for non-tmux operations is out of scope here). - Part of #560 — implements the iTerm2-style `tmux -CC` control-mode integration (sessions/windows → native cmux tabs/splits, attach); remote-first and behind a beta flag, not the local-sidebar drag-drop UX described in the issue. --- Need help on this PR? Tag /codesmith with what you need. Autofix is disabled. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds an opt‑in Remote tmux beta that mirrors a remote `tmux` server over SSH via `cmux ssh-tmux`, mapping sessions to workspaces, windows to tabs, and panes to native splits. Attach is CLI‑only with interactive SSH auth fallback; mirrors aren’t auto‑restored on launch. - **Bug Fixes** - Control stream/backpressure: bounded parser, safe `%begin/%end` correlation with first‑attach block drained, FIFO‑safe queued stdin writer, tighter output buffering, and UTF‑8‑safe `%output`. - Attach/reconnect/sizing: seed‑before‑size with a redraw kick, reliable first‑connect sizing (debounced), live auto‑reconnect with backoff and full reseed, conditional shell/TUI reflow via DECAWM no‑reflow, async resize, alt‑screen enter/leave, and mouse forwarding. - Routing/API: v1/v2 split/create/new‑pane/new‑surface return “accepted, routed to `remote-tmux`”; reject unsupported options (cwd/cmd/env/divider/left‑up) before mutation; prevent orphan local splits; propagate remote send failures; veto batch closes on route failure; scope dedicated‑window ownership; add `remote.tmux.*` methods/policy/capabilities. - Quit/teardown: close the shared SSH ControlMaster on last‑mirror close and on quit (including connection‑only cases); guard against re‑attach races; avoid sticky empty dedicated windows; don’t drop masters still used by an attach connection. - CWD/paste: restore terminal working‑directory inheritance and live updates; upload images to the host over SSH; route single‑line paste/drop via `tmux paste-buffer -p` for bracketed pastes. - UI/perf/docs: avoid main‑thread path stats via a per‑path cache; gate Remote tmux docs/nav to `en`/`ja`; add a Settings search anchor; CLI help for `ssh-tmux`. - Close confirmations: prompt before killing remote tabs/panes with an active command; app/window close detaches instead. Written for commit c690dc74f0d6ba880a4e6f6955b5846f1539ec93. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit # Release Notes * **New Features** * Added "Remote tmux" beta feature for mirroring remote tmux sessions into dedicated local windows or sidebar workspaces via SSH. * Added `cmux ssh-tmux` CLI command with interactive SSH authentication support and customizable port/identity options. * Enabled remote session attachment, splitting, renaming, and pasting with automatic working-directory tracking. * **Documentation** * Added comprehensive Remote tmux documentation with setup instructions, supported behaviors, and limitations. * Added localized UI text in English and Japanese. * **Chores** * Updated project dependencies and Xcode configuration. * Enhanced `.gitignore` for local artifacts.

items.title: Autofix: add PR review autofix pipeline + Windows daemon
items.body:
## Summary

Adds a PR review autofix pipeline that uses the Claude Agent SDK subscription to address review comments automatically, plus a Windows background daemon that runs the loop + supervises the OpenClaw gateway.

- `autofix.py` (~785 lines) — core pipeline: fetches PR review comments, generates minimal fixes via Claude, applies patches on the PR's head branch (fork-aware), replies to each review comment with a summary
- `scripts/autofix_daemon.py` (~800 lines) — background supervisor; runs the autofix loop on an interval AND keeps the OpenClaw gateway alive. Optional ComfyUI window supervisor for image-gen crons
- `scripts/build-autofix-exe.ps1` — PyInstaller build to `dist-autofix/openclaw-autofix.exe` (single-file, no console)
- `scripts/autofix-install-windows-task.ps1` + `-uninstall` — Windows Task Scheduler install/uninstall
- `scripts/autofix-loop.ps1` + `autofix-loop-hidden.vbs` — launcher that hides the console flash
- `.github/workflows/pr-autofix.yml` — CI workflow for running the pipeline on GitHub-hosted runners

## Safety invariants

- **Ping-pong guard** — refuses to post if the last comment was by the autofix bot itself (prevents self-reply loops)
- **Fork-aware push** — discovers `head_repo` from PR info; pushes fixes to the fork that owns the branch, not the base repo
- **SHA-pinned clone** — `git init` + `git fetch --depth=1 origin <sha>` closes the race where the branch could advance between patch generation and clone
- **Per-run `mkdtemp`** workdir with robust Windows cleanup
- **Hidden on Windows** — `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` for subprocess spawns, `--noconsole` on the PyInstaller exe, VBScript launcher wrapper
- **Absolute `node.exe` resolution** — avoids MS Store Python subprocess issues
- **stdin-based prompt delivery** — dodges the 32KB Windows cmdline limit

## Env vars (daemon)

| Name | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GITHUB_TOKEN` | — (required) | PR reads + commit pushes |
| `AUTOFIX_TARGET_REPO` | `openclaw/openclaw` | PR base repo (comments go here) |
| `AUTOFIX_TARGET_PR` | `68135` | PR number to watch |
| `AUTOFIX_INTERVAL_SEC` | `600` | seconds between cycles |
| `AUTOFIX_START_GATEWAY` | `1` | supervise \`openclaw.mjs gateway run\` |
| `AUTOFIX_START_LOOP` | `1` | run the autofix loop |
| `AUTOFIX_COMFYUI` | `0` | optional ComfyUI supervision for image-gen |
| `AUTOFIX_COMFYUI_WINDOW` | — | \`HH:MM-HH:MM\` window to keep ComfyUI up |

All env vars are read from the user-scope registry (`setx`) on startup via a winreg hydration pass, so updated values take effect on the next daemon restart without needing to log out/in.

## Known cleanup before squash-merge

- Commit \`4beee4a6 Follow-up batch: SHA-pinned autofix clone, hook enable-policy, SDK deny enforcement\` — title references "hook enable-policy, SDK deny enforcement" that lived on a separate claude-sdk runtime branch and were dropped during rebase. The remaining content is purely the SHA-pinned autofix clone change. Happy to reword or squash.
- No \`CHANGELOG.md\` entry yet — I held off in case there's a preferred format for new-feature lines. Suggested wording:
  > - PR autofix pipeline: add a Python \`autofix.py\` + Windows daemon that runs PR autofix on an interval using the Agent SDK subscription, with ping-pong guards, fork-targeted pushes, and Windows Task Scheduler install. Opt-in via the \`pr-autofix\` GitHub Actions workflow.

## Test plan

- [x] \`scripts\build-autofix-exe.ps1\` produces a working standalone \`.exe\` (8.4 MB)
- [x] Daemon reads \`GITHUB_TOKEN\`, \`AUTOFIX_TARGET_REPO\`, \`AUTOFIX_TARGET_PR\` from Windows user-scope registry
- [x] Gateway supervisor reclaims port 18789 from a pre-existing openclaw gateway
- [x] Ping-pong guard silent-403s on self-authored comments
- [x] Running on my own Windows 11 workstation as a Startup-folder shortcut
- [ ] CI pipeline (\`pr-autofix.yml\`) workflow run green

items.title: feat: wire cut-release.sh cross-repo publish via gh api (#872)
items.body:
## Summary

Unblocks promotion of the #870 reusables. The six #482 reusables + `feature-ideation` are hosted in `petry-projects/.github`, so their release/channel tags belong on **that** repo — but `cut-release.sh` resolved refs against local git and **refused** live cross-repo cuts (the push target was flagged an open question, `TODO(#872)`). This wires the cross-repo path.

## What changed
- **Cross-repo resolve + publish via `gh api`** — for a `cross_repo_agent`, the ref resolves against `petry-projects/.github` (`commits/<ref>`; an `origin/` prefix is stripped so `origin/main` → its `main`), and `--push` creates the annotated `<name>/vX.Y.Z` release object + force-moves the `<name>/<channel>` tag (`git/tags` + `git/refs`).
- **This-repo agents unchanged** — `pr-review`/`dev-lead` keep the local-git tag+push path verbatim.
- **Immutability preserved cross-repo** — an existing `<name>/vX.Y.Z` is never overwritten.
- `--push` for a cross-repo agent requires `GH_TOKEN` with `contents:write` on `petry-projects/.github`.

## Tests
- `strip_origin` pure helper (+4 cases).
- New gh-mocked integration suite `tests/test_cut_release_cross_repo.bats`: dry-run resolves + touches nothing; print-only (no `--push`); `--push` creates release + moves channel on `.github`; `--push` refuses an existing release tag; this-repo agent still uses local git.
- **46 pass**, `shellcheck --severity=warning` clean.

## Docs
`versioning.md` + `runbook.md` updated — cross-repo cut is now wired (was "dry-run only"). Note: `canary-rollout.sh` (the automated promotion driver) does **not** yet use this cross-repo path, so the six stay out of `canary-rings.json` until that's taught the same move — manual/scripted `cut-release.sh` cuts work today.
